# barndoor_dlp_detection_engine (Resource)

Manages a Data Protection (DLP) detection engine — the platform app calls these **Protection Profiles**: a named binding of a detection provider (`provider_type`) to the detection types it scans for, optionally wired to a named provider connection and provider-specific configuration.

Detection engines are what `barndoor_dlp_enforcement_policy.detection_engine_ids` references. One UI Protection Profile can span several engines that share a `name` across provider types — the uniqueness key is (`name`, `provider_type`) per organization.

Supported `provider_type` values (validated by the API): `builtin_regex`, `builtin_pii_regex`, `builtin_secrets_regex`, `custom_regex`, `presidio`, `gliner`, `rampart`, `google_dlp`, `aws_comprehend_pii`, `azure_ai_language_pii`, `prompt_injection`, `aws_bedrock_guardrails`, `azure_content_safety`, `code_execution`. `code_execution` and `rampart` are feature-gated per organization (the API answers 403 when the organization is not entitled).

## Example Usage

```terraform
# A detection engine ("Protection Profile" in the app) binds a detection
# provider to the detection types it scans for. Engines are unique per
# (name, provider_type) — the same name across provider types renders as one
# merged profile in the app.
resource "barndoor_dlp_detection_engine" "pii" {
  name          = "Corporate PII"
  provider_type = "presidio"

  # Named Data Protection provider connection (for provider types that call
  # an external service); omit for built-in providers.
  provider_connection_name = "primary-presidio"

  enabled_detection_types = [
    "DETECTION_TYPE_EMAIL_ADDRESS",
    "DETECTION_TYPE_PHONE_NUMBER",
  ]

  # Provider-specific configuration; defaults to {} when omitted.
  config = jsonencode({ language = "en" })
}

# Engines are what enforcement policies reference.
resource "barndoor_dlp_enforcement_policy" "tokenize_pii" {
  name   = "Tokenize PII on MCP traffic"
  action = "POLICY_ACTION_TOKENIZE"

  mcp_targets = [
    { mcp_server_id = "*", direction = "BOTH" },
  ]

  detection_engine_ids = [barndoor_dlp_detection_engine.pii.id]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `enabled_detection_types` (List of String) Detection type wire names (`DETECTION_TYPE_…`, including `barndoor_dlp_custom_detection_type.detection_type` values) this engine scans for. At least one is required, and the API rejects names outside the built-in set and the organization's custom detection types.
- `name` (String) Display name of the detection engine (the Protection Profile name in the app). Unique per organization **and** `provider_type` — the same name may exist for several provider types.
- `provider_type` (String) Detection provider backing the engine (see the resource description for the supported values). Changing it updates the engine in place.

### Optional

- `config` (String) Provider-specific engine configuration as JSON (`jsonencode({...})`). The platform stores it verbatim (JSONB) and defaults to `{}` when omitted; removing the attribute resets the configuration to `{}`.
- `provider_connection_name` (String) Name of the Data Protection provider connection the engine uses (for provider types that call an external service, e.g. `presidio` or `google_dlp`). Omit for built-in providers or to use the provider type's default connection.

### Read-Only

- `capabilities` (Attributes) Capability flags of the engine's provider, derived by the platform from `provider_type`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--capabilities))
- `created_at` (String) When the engine was created (RFC 3339).
- `created_by` (String) Subject that created the engine (empty when the platform could not attribute it).
- `id` (String) Detection engine UUID assigned by the API; also the `terraform import` key, and what `barndoor_dlp_enforcement_policy.detection_engine_ids` references.
- `org_id` (String) Organization the detection engine belongs to, resolved from the provider credential's token claims.
- `provider_class` (String) Capability class of the provider: `native`, `span_detection`, or `guardrail_intervention`.
- `runtime_stages` (List of String) Runtime stages the engine can evaluate.
- `supported_actions` (List of String) Enforcement policy actions the engine supports (what `barndoor_dlp_enforcement_policy.action` may be when the policy references this engine).
- `supported_detection_types` (List of String) Every detection type wire name the engine's provider can produce, derived by the platform from its capability tables.
- `updated_at` (String) When the engine was last updated (RFC 3339).
- `updated_by` (String) Subject that last updated the engine.

<a id="nestedatt--capabilities"></a>
### Nested Schema for `capabilities`

Read-Only:

- `confidence_scores` (Boolean) Whether findings carry confidence scores.
- `native_blocking` (Boolean) Whether the provider blocks content natively.
- `native_masking` (Boolean) Whether the provider masks content natively.
- `pii_detection` (Boolean) Whether the provider detects PII.
- `prompt_attack_detection` (Boolean) Whether the provider detects prompt attacks.
- `provider_class` (String) Capability class (same value as the top-level `provider_class`).
- `secret_detection` (Boolean) Whether the provider detects secrets.
- `span_offsets` (Boolean) Whether findings carry span offsets (required for redact/mask).
- `supports_tokenization_pipeline` (Boolean) Whether the engine can feed the tokenization pipeline.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Import by the detection engine's UUID (the resource's id).
terraform import barndoor_dlp_detection_engine.pii 11111111-1111-1111-1111-111111111111
```
